Federal Customer Data: Agency-supplied electronic data excludes provider-generated account/telemetry metadata by default; specific agreements may add protection obligations. Internet-Reachable Vulnerability (IRV): Internet-origin payloads can reach indirectly; classification is specific to the vulnerable machine processing the payload, not the entire network. Likely: Reasonable contextual probability does not prescribe a percentage or scoring product. Likely Exploitable Vulnerability (LEV): Conjunctive not-fully-mitigated, likely-actor reachability and likely adverse effect tests apply; automated unauthenticated internet exploitation is at minimum LEV. Overdue Vulnerability: Intended full resolution that has not or will not meet applicable timeframes includes forecast overdue state, not only past-due tickets. Potential Agency Impact: Cumulative likely effects across agencies govern PAIN; a scanner severity or single-system impact is not automatically equivalent. Responsibly: Judgment includes restraint on adversary-helpful detail and pre-remediation disclosure; optional release still needs a responsible scope decision. Vulnerability: Includes Practice gaps, weak credentials, exposures and process weaknesses as well as software defects; scanner-only coverage is insufficient. Vulnerability Detection: Discovery includes identifying affected resources and varied methods; it is not merely a scan purchase or summary count. Vulnerability Response: Tracking, evaluation, monitoring, mitigation, remediation, exploitation assessment and reporting all remain distinct management activities.
